data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"If the workspace is strictly deterministic and oracle-free, the safest 'reclamation' protocol is trivial\u2014any displacement is detectable by recomputation\u2014so the only necessary durable record is a certificate that the workspace boundary contains no hidden non-deterministic inputs.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Recomputation may be computationally infeasible despite theoretical determinism, making displacement effectively irreversible in practice.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The certificate of oracle-free determinism may be false or unverifiable, giving a false sense of safety.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The problem domain may treat evidence as a social or contractual object whose identity includes the time of completion, not just its content, so recomputation does not replace the original.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The covering principle is that silent displacement of completed evidence is only a safety hazard if the evidence is non-reproducible. A strictly deterministic per-problem workspace produces evidence that is a pure function of the problem input. Therefore, the protocol need only durably record whether the workspace ingested any non-reproducible oracle inputs such as random seeds or wall-clock time. If none, reclamation safety reduces to a liveness concern, not correctness, and the protocol can safely recompute. If oracles exist, their exact values must be durably recorded to make post-crash reproduction possible.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
